_comment: PRD #439 friction baseline — the ledger of CURRENTLY-ACCEPTED friction findings measured against tests/e2e/fixtures/crewops-snapshot via the real CLI sequence. Post-adopt journey on a shared tree: adopt -> heal -> audit --fix -> doctor -> classify --dry-run -> sync --dry-run -> reconcile --dry-run -> upgrade --dry-run -> version --offline -> enforce -> reconform --dry-run -> front door (+ interactive PTY front door); plus alternate-tree captures on their own fresh copies: greet (pre-adopt), init (greenfield), migrate-layout (git-seeded). This is the ratchet: a finding whose key is NOT here is a regression and FAILS the gate. Keys may only be REMOVED across commits, never added — the ONLY sanctioned addition is day-one red recorded when the gate's command surface is first widened, and the #442 monotonic guard enforces that every added key carries a _removal_triggers entry (ADR-0003). Closing a friction-fix issue means deleting its key here AND the gate confirming the finding no longer reproduces (see docs/agents/friction-loop.md).

_removal_triggers.repetition:doctor:- [x] `<path>`: Collapse doctor's per-file '- [x] `<path>`' managed-files checklist to a tier/count summary by default (mirror the heal wall-collapse, #448); full list behind --verbose.
_removal_triggers.next-step-dead-end:run 'claude-ds audit': reconcile/upgrade/version suggest 'run claude-ds audit' as a → Next: step, but audit is read-only and changes no state, so the liveness runner reads it as a dead end. Fix by either dropping the suggestion when the tree is already clean, or pointing at an action that actually advances state.
_removal_triggers.repetition:sync:skip: <path> — in sync: Collapse sync's per-file 'skip: <path> — in sync' wall to a count by default (the ~40-line block buries the one 'rewrite:' line that matters); full list behind --verbose, mirroring the heal/doctor wall-collapse.
_removal_triggers.repetition:sync:skip: <path> — seeded; n: Collapse sync's per-file 'skip: <path> — seeded; never re-touched' wall to a count by default; full list behind --verbose.
_removal_triggers.self-block:sync->heal: sync leaves managed writes in the tree, then a bare heal refuses on the dirty tree — the suggested sequence wedges itself. Fix by having heal tolerate its own pipeline's managed writes (it already runs sub-commands with --allow-dirty internally) or by not steering the user from sync into a heal that will refuse.
_removal_triggers.repetition:reconform:[backfill-companion: reconform echoes the full diff-style stub SOURCE of every backfilled companion (19 here — the gate's injected brownfield atoms amplify the count), producing walls of near-identical lines. Collapse reconform's backfill output to a per-file count/summary by default; show the generated source behind --verbose. All repetition:reconform:* keys burn down together when this lands.

Either drop the '→ Next:' prefix for non-command guidance, or replace it with a concrete runnable suggestion.
_removal_triggers.next-step-dead-end:run 'claude-ds heal': migrate-layout ends with '→ Next: run claude-ds heal to converge the project to clean', but heal exits 1 (non-converged — it fails loudly per the completeness principle) on the post-migrate-layout tree, so the suggestion dead-ends. Fix by ensuring the suggested heal can actually converge from that state, or by making migrate-layout's next-step reflect what will actually succeed.
